newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, underperform Dow.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, underperform Dow.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Monday, ignoring gains in New York and higher gold prices that lifted Canadian gold stocks.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 54.78 points to finish at 6840.37. More than 82 million shares were traded worth C$1.48 billion ($1 billion).
"I think we had a bit of a buyer's strike ahead of (U.S. and Canadian) economic data this week," one Canadian stock trader said.
Canadian new motor vehicle sales are due on Wednesday.
U.S. producer price data for July are also due on Wednesday, followed by July consumer price numbers on Thursday.
While Canada's biggest stock market languished on Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed almost 31 points.
All but one of Toronto's 14 sectors finished lower.
Precious metals added 58 points as COMEX gold futures rose on uncertainty over the direction of U.S. stocks and bonds. COMEX October gold gained $2.10 to $330.40 an ounce on Monday.
But the strength in golds was overwhelmed by weak interest in rate-sensitive issues, including financial services and utilities.

* CGI Group class A fell 15.75 to 27 in very light volume. CGI said it would acquire Teleglobe Inc.'s Insurance Systems group for C$20 million ($14 million) cash and C$120 million ($86 million) in first preferred shares worth C$45.58 ($32.70) a share on a pre-split basis.
* Among rate-sensitive issues, communications giant BCE Inc fell 0.85 to 41.20. Royal Bank of Canada also lost 0.85 to finish at 64.65.
* Royal Oak Mines Inc. slipped 0.04 to 2.52 after forecasting a break-even 1998 and a return to profit in 1999.
* ATS Automation Tooling Systems Inc. jumped 4.75 to 41.75 after reporting higher first-quarter earnings.
